core_claim: Black Summer's first week was not a freak event — it was the visible mid-air collision of a century of warming, a year of record drought, and a wave of 511,661-hectare megafires that satellites could already see lighting up Australia's south-east before most of the world noticed.

edt_01.label: The week the satellites lit up
edt_01.title: The week the satellites lit up
edt_01.editorial_notes: Lead with the satellite map — the visceral overhead view. The 34,248 detections and 59% Victoria share are the framing numbers.

edt_02.label: Sixty percent burned at night
edt_02.title: Sixty percent of Victoria's fires burned at night
edt_02.editorial_notes: Night burning is an under-appreciated mechanism — 60.6% Victorian night share is the standout number. FRP tail and brightness-cluster (East Gippsland → Mallacoota) carry forward.

edt_03.label: The driest year, almost everywhere
edt_03.title: The driest year, almost everywhere
edt_03.editorial_notes: 61% of average is the headline. The November/December collapse story (ana_06) is the mechanism.

edt_04.label: A century of warming, then 2019
edt_04.title: A century of warming, then 2019
edt_04.editorial_notes: 26.4 C is the load-bearing 2019 anomaly. Decadal city deltas (Canberra +2.39, Perth +2.10) anchor the long-run warming.

edt_05.label: 4 million hectares, before the season ended
edt_05.title: Four million hectares, in one state, on one day
edt_05.editorial_notes: Gospers Mountain 511,661 ha is the centrepiece individual story. NSW 4.0 Mha vs season-long 24 Mha gives the proportional gut-punch.

edt_06.label: What the dataset is, and what it is not
edt_06.title: What the dataset is, and what it is not
edt_06.editorial_notes: Honest close. MODIS is not ground truth. TidyTuesday's own warning is the kicker. Do not invent new numbers in this section.
